title: FLEX Spherical Droplet Flame in Microgravity
description: True color high-speed video frame of an isolated n-heptane droplet burning in microgravity aboard the ISS. In the absence of buoyancy-driven natural convection, the flame assumes near-perfect spherical symmetry around the evaporating droplet.
apparatus: MDCA / CIR on ISS (Quiescent Stagnant Chamber, 21% O2, 1.0 atm)
source_citation: Nayagam, V., Dietrich, D. L., Hicks, M. C., & Williams, F. A. (2012). Combustion and Flame, 159(11), 3406-3414.
comparison_axis_note: Comparison of zero-g spherical symmetry vs terrestrial 1-g buoyant plume elongation under identical fuel and droplet diameter.

annotations.label: Liquid Droplet Core
annotations.description: Evaporating liquid heptane droplet supported on a 14-micron SiC filament.

annotations.label: Inner Reaction Zone
annotations.description: Spherical high-temperature blue chemiluminescence zone where vaporized fuel and diffused oxygen react stoichiometrically.

annotations.label: Soot Annulus / Radiative Shell
annotations.description: Concentric yellow-orange soot shell where unoxidized carbon agglomerates accumulate due to lack of buoyant escape.

title: Terrestrial 1-g Baseline Droplet Flame (Buoyant Updraft)
description: Ground-based calibration frame of an n-heptane droplet burning in Earth gravity (1-g). Strong buoyant convection draws air upward, elongating the flame into an upright teardrop geometry with an unsteady flickering tip.
apparatus: NASA Glenn 1-g Droplet Combustion Rig (Quiescent, 21% O2, 1.0 atm)
source_citation: Nayagam, V., et al. (2012). Droplet Extinction in Normal and Reduced Gravity. Combustion and Flame.
comparison_axis_note: Direct terrestrial contrast to microgravity droplet flame.

annotations.label: Droplet Base
annotations.description: Liquid fuel droplet tethered at bottom of buoyant convective envelope.

annotations.label: Elongated Buoyant Plume
annotations.description: Teardrop flame envelope narrowed and pulled upward by gravity-driven density difference.

annotations.label: Flickering Soot Tail
annotations.description: Rapid convective exhaust carrying soot particles upward through open flame tip.

title: FLEX Low-Temperature 'Cool Flame' Radiative Transition
description: Infrared and radiometric false-color composite of an n-heptane droplet following hot-flame extinction at t = 4.1 s. A non-luminous low-temperature chemical reaction zone (600–1000 K) sustains quasi-steady evaporation without visible emissions.
apparatus: MDCA / CIR on ISS (Chamber at 21% O2, 10% CO2, 1.0 atm)
source_citation: Williams, F. A., & Nayagam, V. (2013). Cool flame burning of alkanes in microgravity. Microgravity Science and Technology.
comparison_axis_note: Comparison between high-temperature visible combustion (t=2.4s) and low-temperature invisible cool-flame combustion (t=4.1s).

annotations.label: Droplet Core (Cool Phase)
annotations.description: Droplet continues losing mass despite absence of visible flame.

annotations.label: Low-Temperature Reaction Shell
annotations.description: Peroxide-driven low-temperature kinetic zone (~750 K) producing zero visual light.

title: SAFFIRE-I Ignition Transient on Cygnus OA-6 (t = 15 s)
description: High-definition flow duct camera frame capturing ignition of a 0.4 m x 0.94 m SIBAL composite fabric sheet aboard the uncrewed Cygnus OA-6 spacecraft. A hot-wire igniter initiates flame propagation under 20 cm/s concurrent airflow.
fuel_or_material: SIBAL fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass, 0.4 x 0.94 m)
apparatus: Saffire Flow Duct (20 cm/s forced airflow, cabin air, 101.3 kPa)
source_citation: Urban, D. L., Ruff, G. A., et al. (2017). Large-scale Spacecraft Fire Safety Testing: The Saffire-I Flight Experiment. NASA/TM-2017-219502.
comparison_axis_note: Direct time-series comparison: Ignition transient at t=15s versus quasi-steady concurrent spread at t=180s.

annotations.label: Hot-Wire Igniter Line
annotations.description: Electric resistance wire igniter positioned at upstream edge of fabric sample.

annotations.label: Forced Airflow Vector
annotations.description: 20 cm/s forced ventilation entering from left duct flow straightener.

title: SAFFIRE-I Quasi-Steady Concurrent Flame Spread (t = 180 s)
description: Flow duct camera frame at peak combustion (t = 180 s). Flame front propagates steadily at 1.8 mm/s along the SIBAL fabric. Thermocouple readings behind the flame front reached 910 °C with radiant heat flux exceeding 6.1 kW/m².
apparatus: Saffire Flow Duct (20 cm/s forced airflow, cabin air, 101.3 kPa)
source_citation: Urban, D. L., Ruff, G. A., et al. (2017). Saffire-I Flight Experiment. NASA/TM-2017-219502.
comparison_axis_note: Shows transition from initial ignition to fully developed concurrent flame spread.

annotations.label: Active Flame Front
annotations.description: Concurrent flame boundary advancing with forced airflow at 1.8 mm/s.

annotations.label: Pyrolysis Zone
annotations.description: Solid fabric decomposition zone releasing combustible volatile hydrocarbons.

annotations.label: Fiberglass Char Lattice
annotations.description: Non-combustible woven fiberglass backing that retains char and prevents burning debris release.

title: SAFFIRE-I Post-Burn Char & Structural Retention Matrix (t = 450 s)
description: Post-extinction inspection frame at t = 450 s. All combustible cotton has pyrolyzed while the fiberglass grid remained intact across the entire 0.94 m length, proving structural retention under spacecraft duct flow.
source_citation: Urban, D. L., et al. (2017). Saffire-I Flight Experiment. NASA/TM-2017-219502.
comparison_axis_note: Comparison of peak flame spread against post-extinction residual char structure.

annotations.label: Consumed Fuel Zone
annotations.description: 94 cm sample fully pyrolyzed; ambient oxygen dropped from 20.95% to 18.79%.

title: SPICE Laminar Closed-Tip Jet Flame (Below Smoke Point)
description: Color-ratio pyrometry camera frame of an ethylene jet diffusion flame in microgravity at 10 cm/s co-flow velocity. The flame tip remains fully closed with complete soot oxidation within the flame envelope.
apparatus: ACME / CIR on ISS (Laminar Co-flow Air Duct at 10 cm/s, 101.3 kPa)
source_citation: Sunderland, P. B., Urban, D. L., Axelbaum, R. L., & Chao, B. H. (2018). Proceedings of the Combustion Institute, 37(2), 2045-2053.
comparison_axis_note: Comparison between non-smoking closed tip (below smoke point) and open smoking tip (above smoke point) under co-flow.

annotations.label: Fuel Jet Nozzle
annotations.description: 1.6 mm brass burner nozzle issuing ethylene gas.

annotations.label: Closed Luminous Tip
annotations.description: Parabolic flame boundary completely enclosing reaction products; zero smoke emission.

title: SPICE Smoking Flame Tip (Above Smoke Point Threshold)
description: Pyrometry camera frame of an ethylene jet flame exceeding its laminar smoke point (fuel flow rate 2.32 mg/s, 30 cm/s co-flow). Lengthened soot residence time prevents complete oxidation, causing soot particle breakthrough at the flame tip.
apparatus: ACME / CIR on ISS (Laminar Co-flow Air Duct at 30 cm/s, 101.3 kPa)
source_citation: Sunderland, P. B., et al. (2018). Laminar smoke points in microgravity. Proc. Combust. Inst.
comparison_axis_note: Direct morphological evidence of soot breakthrough above the critical smoke-point threshold.

annotations.label: Soot Breakthrough Zone
annotations.description: Tip rupture point where unoxidized soot aggregates escape into co-flow duct.

annotations.label: Soot Emission Plume
annotations.description: Aerosolized soot particles drifting toward spacecraft detection duct.

title: BASS PMMA Cylindrical Rod Combustion in Low-Speed Flow Duct
description: High-resolution video frame of a 12.7 mm diameter cast PMMA rod burning inside the BASS flow duct aboard the ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox. Shows the rounded leading flame base and molten pyrolyzing fuel layer under 2.0 cm/s forced airflow.
apparatus: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / BASS Flow Duct (21% O2, 1.0 atm)
source_citation: Ferkul, P. V., Olson, S. L., & T'ien, J. S. (2014). Combustion and Flame, 161(11), 2975-2983.
comparison_axis_note: Comparison of steady polymeric flame spread under forced airflow vs nitrogen dilution extinction boundary.

annotations.label: Hemispherical Flame Base
annotations.description: Leading edge blue chemiluminescent flame anchor stabilized against the incoming 2.0 cm/s flow.

annotations.label: Bubbling Pyrolysis Layer
annotations.description: Sub-surface boiling and depolymerization of PMMA into methyl methacrylate monomer vapor.

annotations.label: Thermocouple Array
annotations.description: Rake sensor measuring peak gas flame temperatures exceeding 815 °C.

title: BASS Nitrogen Dilution Extinction at Limiting Oxygen Index (LOI)
description: Extinction boundary sequence showing flame detachment and thermal quench of a PMMA rod following gaseous nitrogen injection into the ISS MSG duct as oxygen concentration falls below 15.5%.
apparatus: ISS Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) / BASS Flow Duct (15.5% O2, 1.0 atm)
source_citation: Ferkul, P. V., Olson, S. L., & T'ien, J. S. (2014). Combustion and Flame, 161(11), 2975-2983.
comparison_axis_note: Visual confirmation of nitrogen dilution suppression and flame lift-off at the limiting oxygen index.

annotations.label: Detached Flame Boundary
annotations.description: Receding reaction zone lifting off the rod surface due to insufficient chemical reaction rate.

annotations.label: Extinguished Surface Char
annotations.description: Quenched solid fuel tip with no remaining visible or radiant combustion activity.

title: FLEX-2 Binary Droplet Two-Stage Hot and Cool Flame
description: Intensified ICCD camera frame of a binary heptane/hexadecane droplet burning in the CIR MDCA on the ISS, displaying the concentric hot-flame extinction boundary and sustained inner cool flame reaction zone.
apparatus: MDCA / CIR on ISS (Quiescent Stagnant Chamber, 21% O2, 1.0 atm)
camera_modality: Intensified OH* Chemiluminescence ICCD (308 nm narrow band)
source_citation: Dietrich, D. L., Nayagam, V., Hicks, M. C., & Williams, F. A. (2017). Microgravity Sci. Technol., 29(3), 201-212.
comparison_axis_note: Comparison of single-stage pure alkane droplet burning (FLEX) vs two-stage binary cool-flame persistence (FLEX-2).

annotations.label: Binary Droplet Core
annotations.description: Liquid fuel core with preferential vaporization of volatile n-heptane.

annotations.label: Sustained Cool Flame Shell
annotations.description: Low-temperature reaction zone (600-850 K) burning without visible soot.

annotations.label: Extinguished Hot Flame Boundary
annotations.description: Outer radius where visible high-temperature combustion extinguished radiatively.

title: SAFFIRE-II Multi-Material Spacecraft Flammability Card
description: Composite imaging frame of the SAFFIRE-II multi-sample flammability experiment aboard Cygnus OA-5, comparing flame spread rates across concurrent SIBAL fabric, PMMA sheet, and self-extinguished Nomex.
fuel_or_material: SIBAL fabric, PMMA sheet, and Nomex strips
apparatus: Cygnus OA-5 Post-Departure Vehicle Flow Duct (20 cm/s airflow, 21% O2)
source_citation: Urban, D. L., Ruff, G. A., et al. (2017). Saffire-II Multi-Sample Results. 47th ICES.
comparison_axis_note: Comparison of single-sample large-scale fabric spread (SAFFIRE-I) vs comparative multi-material flammability (SAFFIRE-II).

annotations.label: SIBAL Flame Front
annotations.description: Rapid concurrent fabric flame spread reaching 1.75 mm/s.

annotations.label: PMMA Solid Sheet Spread
annotations.description: Slower solid polymer flame spread (0.58 mm/s) accompanied by surface bubbling.

annotations.label: Nomex Self-Extinction Zone
annotations.description: Inherent fire-retardant aramid fabric self-extinguishing immediately adjacent to igniter.
